messages:
jess (Customer): Hey team — just had a user hit duplicate generations + partial output after a reconnect. They reported being billed twice for the same prompt. Happened over SSE streaming when mobile app lost LTE for ~3s and reconnected. Request id = req_0a9f3b. Model: gpt-open-16k; streaming via SSE. Attached short client log: 

jess (Customer): [client log] 
CONNECT -> chunk(0..512) final:false
DISCONNECT (network)
RECONNECT -> resend chunk(0..512) -> server responded with continuation chunk(512..1024) but client displayed both chunks twice.

jess (Customer): Not sure if client double-sent or server resumed incorrectly. Customer is upset about billing. Can you advise? :frowning:

sara (CS): thanks — sorry about that. can you paste the full request headers (no secrets) and the exact timestamps? also did the client include an idempotency key or resume token?

jess (Customer): headers: 
Authorization: Bearer sk-****
Accept: text/event-stream
Idempotency-Key: (none)
X-Client-Version: myapp/2.4.1

jess (Customer): timestamps (local): 2024-05-22T16:18:02Z disconnect, reconnect attempt 2024-05-22T16:18:05Z, stream resumed 16:18:06Z. no idempotency key used.

mike (Eng): probable root cause: client re-sent the last in-flight bytes after reconnect without an idempotency/resume token. server resumes but also processed the re-sent fragment as new input, causing duplicate tokens. can you share the exact payload snapshot (first ~300 bytes) and the server-assigned resume token if present?

jess (Customer): payload snippet: 
POST /v1/streams/generate
{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following..."}],"stream":true} 

jess (Customer): we don't see a resume token in the response (client didn't persist any). client just re-opened the SSE connection and replayed the last buffer on reconnect for reliability.

dan (Infra): that replay behavior is dangerous without an idempotency key. we have two mitigations: server-side resume token semantics (recommended) or enforce idempotency-key at ingress for streaming sessions so duplicate request IDs are rejected for a small window. for this customer i can temporarily enable session dedupe by mapping connection session -> request_id for 30s to prevent double billing while we investigate. :thumbsup:

mike (Eng): repro suggestion for the team: run this curl sequence to simulate the client re-send: 

```
# open stream
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Test duplicate"}],"stream":true}' -o stream.out &
# simulate disconnect (kill curl) then immediately re-send same payload without idempotency-key
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/generate -d '{"messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Test duplicate"}],"stream":true}' -o stream2.out
```

mike (Eng): if stream2.out contains tokens that were already emitted to stream.out you can reproduce. this matches what the customer saw when mobile replayed buffered bytes.

sara (CS): next steps for support: 
- (sara) escalate billing for req_0a9f3b, issue credit for duplicate charge.
- (mike) collect server logs around req_0a9f3b (ingress id, session_id, any resume-token).
- (dan) enable temporary session dedupe for the customer and add a short policy to reject immediate replays without idempotency-key.

support-bot: CREATED TICKET INC-12345 for billing credit and engineering investigation.

jess (Customer): thanks — appreciate the quick action. we'll try to patch the mobile client to keep a resume-token and avoid blind replays. do you have recommended client behavior?

mike (Eng): recommended client pattern: 
- persist server-provided resume-token for the session and send it on reconnect (Resume-Token header). 
- if resume-token not present, include an Idempotency-Key for the entire user request before retrying. 
- avoid blindly replaying in-flight byte ranges; instead resume playback from server ack offsets when available.

dan (Infra): temporary mitigation applied. enabled 30s dedupe window for this org id=org_77b. I'll drop logs to the ticket.

sara (CS): i'll follow up with customer tomorrow with the credit details and a short explainer for the mobile team. tagging @mike (Eng) and @dan (Infra) to confirm when logs uploaded. :eyes:
